plain.text: Joseph threw himself on his father, wept over him and kissed him. He had the physicians embalm Jacob, which took forty days, and the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days. Pharaoh let Joseph go to bury his father in Canaan. A great company went with him: Pharaoh's officials, the leaders of Egypt and all Joseph's household. They mourned at the threshing floor of Atad for seven days. Jacob's sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, as he had asked. Then they returned to Egypt.

Now that their father was dead, Joseph's brothers said, "What if Joseph holds a grudge and pays us back for all the wrong we did?" They sent word to Joseph, saying their father had asked him to forgive them, and they came and threw themselves down before him: "We are your slaves." Joseph wept. "Don't be afraid. Am I in the place of God? As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good, in order to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives. So don't be afraid. I will provide for you and your children." He reassured them and spoke kindly to them.

Joseph stayed in Egypt with his father's family and lived 110 years. He saw his great-grandchildren. He told his brothers, "I am about to die, but God will surely come to your aid and bring you up out of this land to the land he promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob." He made them swear to carry his bones up from Egypt. Joseph died and was embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt.

summary.bigIdea: Joseph forgives his brothers fully: what they meant for evil, God meant for good. Genesis ends with hope that God will bring his people home.
points: Jacob is buried in Canaan with great mourning.
Joseph's brothers fear revenge, but he reassures them: "Don't be afraid."
"What you intended against me for evil, God intended for good." Joseph dies trusting God's promise.
summary.reflection: Joseph said, "Am I in the place of God?" and chose to forgive. How might leaving judgement to God help you forgive?
